objective: Find controlled evidence about whether multi-agent scientific role decomposition materially improves scientific-task quality or efficiency relative to a simpler single-agent baseline.

slice.question: Does primary evidence show that a multi-agent scientific workflow can outperform a single-agent baseline on a matched scientific-analysis task, and what limits that claim?

problem_count_forecast.forecast_note: This bounded slice tests multi-agent versus single-agent evidence on causal discovery only; isolating persistent-state effects remains one explicit child problem.

direct_solution_first.reason: A primary causal-discovery paper provides dataset-level single-agent versus multi-agent comparisons with clear wins on some datasets, but the advantage is not uniform and the specialist-role contribution is not perfectly isolated from tooling and orchestration effects.

candidate_pattern.name: bounded specialist debate/coding decomposition with minimal adversarial coordination
components: simple single-agent fallback when the baseline is already strong
candidate_pattern.clean_boundary_note: This is an external design-pattern candidate only. It does not authorize consumption of O, other workers, downstream state, legacy state, or a shared exploration ledger.

public_primary_evidence.source: Multi-Agent Causal Discovery Using Large Language Models
observations: Auto MPG: the reported single-agent GPT-4o baseline has SHD 8 and F1 0.307, while Coding Agents has SHD 4 and F1 0.526 and Meta Agents has SHD 5 and F1 0.545.
DWD climate: the reported single-agent GPT-4o baseline has SHD 11 and F1 0, while Meta Agents has SHD 5 and F1 0.222; reported hybrid multi-agent variants reach F1 values from 0.182 to 0.307.

Sachs protein is a counterexample to a uniform multi-agent advantage: the reported single-agent GPT-4o baseline has SHD 18, lower than the shown multi-agent variants, although some multi-agent variants have higher F1.

public_primary_evidence.source: Updated OpenReview version of Multi-Agent Causal Discovery Using Large Language Models
observations: The updated paper explicitly evaluates a MAC-Single-Agent ablation, module-only variants, and debate-round count.
Its reported debate-round study indicates that most datasets stabilize after one complete debate round, while additional rounds mainly fluctuate and can degrade Survey and Auto performance.
The updated paper reports that the full multi-agent system can use roughly 16x to 25x more tokens than standard baselines, with coding/debugging accounting for up to about half of consumption.
public_primary_evidence.scope_note: The accessible public snippet truncates the exact numeric conclusion of the MAC-Single-Agent ablation, so this slice does not claim a precise MAC-versus-MAC-Single-Agent delta.

benchmark_assessment.positive_signal: On Auto MPG and DWD climate, reported multi-agent variants materially improve structural-error and/or F1 metrics relative to the single-agent GPT-4o baseline.
benchmark_assessment.counter_signal: On Sachs protein, the single-agent GPT-4o baseline has the best reported SHD among the shown methods, so multi-agent orchestration is not uniformly superior.
benchmark_assessment.causal_attribution_limit: The evidence supports task-level value for multi-agent orchestration on some datasets, but it does not cleanly isolate specialist-role decomposition or persistent state from model, coding-tool, and workflow effects.

negative_evidence_and_limits: The multi-agent advantage is dataset-dependent rather than universal; Sachs protein is an explicit counterexample on SHD.
The updated system's reported 16x to 25x token overhead makes zero-finite-quota and zero-incremental-cost admissibility unproven for the published implementation.
Persistent world state or memory is not isolated by this comparison, so the previous checkpoint's persistent-state child problem remains open.
The exact MAC-versus-MAC-Single-Agent numeric delta was not recovered from the accessible public snippet and is not inferred here.

inference.candidate_value: Use bounded one-round role separation, critique, and coding only when task structure provides measurable gains; retain a simpler single-agent or verifier-centric fallback where a matched baseline is already strong.
inference.why_not_high: Performance is heterogeneous across datasets, role specialization is not independently ablated, and the published resource footprint is not Phase-1 admissible as-is.

decomposition_on_failure.child_problem: Separate the value of persistent research state from role specialization, and find a resource-admissible controlled comparison under the zero-finite-quota and zero-incremental-cost Phase-1 gate.

transversal_on_overrun.reason: Observed active problem count did not exceed the one-leaf forecast during this bounded slice.

expected_completion_forecast.next_slice_target: Audit one primary ablation isolating persistent memory/world state or a lower-cost verifier-centric workflow against a matched single-agent baseline.

alternative_method_on_overrun.fallback: If persistent-state attribution remains unavailable, compare a verifier/critic-only scientific workflow against full multi-agent orchestration using primary controlled evidence.

handoff_target: integrator via CLEAN safe summaries only
continuation: Next invocation: audit one primary controlled comparison isolating persistent research state/memory or a lower-cost verifier-centric workflow against a matched single-agent, preserve CLEAN boundaries, and reject any design whose measured resource footprint violates the zero-finite-quota or zero-incremental-cost Phase-1 gate.
